_comment: DigitalLocks risk weights. Editable. Sum determines riskScore; bands map score to riskLevel. Weights match the V1 spec in DIGITAL_LOCKS_MODULE.md. AFTERHOURS_EDGE has TWO discounted forms, because they rest on different evidence: AFTERHOURS_EDGE_EXPECTED (10) applies when the Position matches role_zone_rules.json::expectedEdgeHourPositions — a generalisation about a job code — while AFTERHOURS_EDGE_HABITUAL (0) applies when calibration has learned that THIS associate actually works these hours, in their own area, across days of the import. A demonstrated pattern is the stronger claim, so it scores nothing; the job-code guess keeps a small residue. Both require the role/zone check to ALSO pass. Delete either key to fall back to the full AFTERHOURS_EDGE weight. Neither ever applies to the deep 12am-5am band.
_inertWeights: NEW_HIRE_CONTEXT (and thresholds.newHireThresholdDays) are NOT read by any rule — no code path applies them, so editing the number changes nothing. The Power BI export carries no hire date, so the rule needs a tenure source first. Kept rather than deleted so the intent isn't lost. See CURRENT_TASKS.md::Watch list. ORDER_NO_MATCH is live but is applied in view.js during the order cross-reference, not in riskScoring.js::scoreEvents.

timeWindows._comment: Local-time hour ranges, 0-23. `deepAfterHours` is the high-severity overnight band; `edgeAfterHours` is the medium-severity early/late bands.

thresholds._comment: Volume rule kicks in when a user's per-day unlock count exceeds BOTH the high-water percentile across all (user,day) pairs in the import AND the absolute floor (so a 5-event day in a quiet file isn't flagged). The percentile is only the FALLBACK now — see calibration.userBaseline.

calibration._comment: Makes rules score DEVIATION FROM OBSERVED NORMAL instead of absolute attributes. Added 2026-08-22 after a 500-event store-1458 import in which every single row was in one high-risk zone: HIGH_RISK_ZONE fired on 100% of rows, adding a flat +20 to everything and pushing the whole store past the Watch band. A reason that describes every event describes none of them. Set enabled=false to restore the old absolute behaviour exactly.

baseRate._comment: Scales a rule's weight down as the share of events it fires on rises. At or below suppressAbove the weight is untouched; at or above zeroAt it contributes nothing; linear in between. Suppressed reasons are still shown on the event as CONTEXT (baselineReasons) — they are just not scored. minEvents stops a 12-row test import from zeroing every rule.

pinnedRules._comment: Rule names listed here keep their full weight no matter how often they fire — the config override on top of the learned behaviour. Use it for anything that must always score, e.g. ["AFTERHOURS_DEEP"]. Deep after-hours is pinned by default: a store where 3am openings are routine is a finding, not a new baseline.

userBaseline._comment: Per-associate normal, learned from the import. volumeMultiple: flag a day only when it exceeds this multiple of THAT user's own median day (Ashley at 20/day against her own median of 19 is not an outlier; the old store-wide p95 flagged her every day for doing her job). shiftPadHours widens the learned first/last working hour before an edge-hours event counts as outside their pattern. minDaysForBaseline / minEventsForBaseline: below these a user has too little history to have a 'normal', and the store-wide fallback is used instead — this is what stops one 3am event from establishing 3am as someone's pattern.

observedRolePairing._comment: A (position → zone) pairing seen this often, from this many distinct people, is how the store actually runs — not a mismatch. At store 1458 Hardlines TAs open the electronics desk constantly because those areas overlap and TAs cover each other; 116 events across multiple associates is an operating pattern, and calling each one an exception buries the one that isn't. Rarer pairings still score. Set minEvents very high to disable.
